dedupe_keys.name: seed platform standard energy efficiency data

description: The Standard Energy Efficiency Data (SEED) Platform is open-source software for managing building performance data, such as the data required by benchmarking ordinances, which states, local governments and other organisations otherwise find costly and time-consuming to handle. It helps users combine data from multiple sources, clean and validate them, and generate queries and reports, and it is funded by the U.S. Department of Energy. SEED is a server-based web application written with the Django Python framework on PostgreSQL; end users reach it through approved hosting providers (technical allies), who may only make branding or plug-in changes to the core code, or through a DOE or national laboratory hosted instance, while organisations can also self-host, with Amazon Web Services the preferred and only tested cloud and a Docker route for Windows. Coverage: designed for U.S. benchmarking programmes; data are those loaded by each user. Access: free open-source code, with accounts from hosting providers. Licence: BSD-style, copyright 2017-2026 Alliance for Energy Innovation and contributors. Caveats: it is a data management tool, not a model, and the hosting page linked from the menu returned 'not found'. Simulation uses: cleaned city benchmarking portfolios as inputs to building stock energy and retrofit models. Related records: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the New York City and Seattle benchmarking datasets.
